[15] user: changed this: What changed

Composer ported from web (components/Composer.tsx) — bordered card holding a + actions menu, the input, and a single send-or-stop control that never shows both, with the web's teaching reminder underneath ("keating won't give you the answer — that's the point"). The menu carries Live, Model, and Thinking. The web's right-hand "enter to send" hint is omitted because web hides it on mobile too.

Light mode — theme preference (System/Light/Dark) in a new UiSettingsProvider layered above the theme provider so the stored choice is known before first paint. This surfaced a real bug: the accent green is only contrast-validated as a background, but was used as text colour throughout — 3.04:1 on the light surface. Added a primaryText role (accentText, 4.96:1) and moved every text/icon usage onto it; dark mode is pixel-identical since the two roles coincide there. Splash now has a light default with a dark variant.

Settings — Appearance (theme, font), Chat (interactive cards, raw provider errors, thinking budget), About You. Each is wired to real behaviour rather than stored and ignored:
- Font installs JetBrains Mono + Roboto and flows typography through the theme (theme.type), so the setting restyles the whole app.
- Thinking budget maps per provider (OpenAI reasoning.effort, Anthropic thinking.budget_tokens with max_tokens raised above it and temperature yielded, Gemini thinkingConfig) and is only sent for models the catalog says support it. While adding this I found Gemini's thought parts would have leaked into replies — now filtered in both the streaming and non-streaming parsers.
- Raw errors keeps the provider's text and derives a friendly summary when off, so the toggle works retroactively on an error already on screen.
- About You appends to the system prompt as JSON-fenced background, mirroring the web's framing so it can't override the teaching protocol.

Live — off the tab bar, entered from the composer. Note the Live screen itself is unchanged: it still explains native Live isn't in this build and links to web. I only moved the entry point, as asked.

Courses — native client: /session, list, join-by-code, and course detail with modules, expandable lessons, materials, and members. Teacher access is an explicit opt-in switch on the join sheet, never implied by joining. "Study this with Keating" handch exposed a latent bug wherenewSession() followed by sendMessage() in one tick posted into the previous session; the state ref now        updates synchronously.
                                                                                                              Two things worth flagging: the web settoxy, share links, animation renderer,flashcards, artifact toggles) per your scope choice, and course authoring/discussion/review remain web-only — the detail screen says so and links outwise. Cookie handling uses an explicitjar rather than trusting RN's native persistence; I haven't run it against a live server, so that's the piece I'd verify first on device.

declare module 'node-pty' {
  /**
   * Forks a process as a pseudoterminal.
   * @param file The file to launch.
   * @param args The file's arguments as argv (string[]) or in a pre-escaped CommandLine format
   * (string). Note that the CommandLine option is only available on Windows and is expected to be
   * escaped properly.
   * @param options The options of the terminal.
   * @see CommandLineToArgvW https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/bb776391(v=vs.85).aspx
   * @see Parsing C++ Comamnd-Line Arguments https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/17w5ykft.aspx
   * @see GetCommandLine https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/ms683156.aspx
   */
  export function spawn(file: string, args: string[] | string, options: IPtyForkOptions | IWindowsPtyForkOptions): IPty;

  export interface IBasePtyForkOptions {

    /**
     * Name of the terminal to be set in environment ($TERM variable).
     */
    name?: string;

    /**
     * Number of intial cols of the pty.
     */
    cols?: number;

    /**
     * Number of initial rows of the pty.
     */
    rows?: number;

    /**
     * Working directory to be set for the child program.
     */
    cwd?: string;

    /**
     * Environment to be set for the child program.
     */
    env?: { [key: string]: string | undefined };

    /**
     * String encoding of the underlying pty.
     * If set, incoming data will be decoded to strings and outgoing strings to bytes applying this encoding.
     * If unset, incoming data will be delivered as raw bytes (Buffer type).
     * By default 'utf8' is assumed, to unset it explicitly set it to `null`.
     */
    encoding?: string | null;

    /**
     * (EXPERIMENTAL)
     * Whether to enable flow control handling (false by default). If enabled a message of `flow<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="827" />oid;

    /**
     * Clears the pty's internal representation of its buffer. This is a no-op
     * unless on Windows/ConPTY. This is useful if the buffer is cleared on the
     * frontend in order to synchronize state with the backend to avoid ConPTY
     * possibly reprinting the screen.
     */
    clear(): void;

    /**
     * Writes data to the pty.
     * @param data The data to write.
     */
    write(data: string | Buffer): void;

    /**
     * Kills the pty.
     * @param signal The signal to use, defaults to SIGHUP. This parameter is not supported on
     * @returns Object with `cancelled: true` if an extension cancelled the clone
     */
    clone(): Promise<{
        cancelled: boolean;
    }>;
    /**
     * Get messages available for forking.
     */
    getForkMessages(): Promise<Array<{
        entryId: string;
        text: string;
    }>>;
    /**
     * Get text of last assistant message.
     */
    getLastAssistantText(): Promise<string | null>;
    /**
     * Set the session display name.
     */
    setSessionName(name: string): Promise<void>;
    /**
     * Get all messages in the session.
     */
    getMessages(): Promise<AgentMessage[]>;
    /**
     * Get available commands (extension commands, prompt templates, skills).
     */
    getCommands(): Promise<RpcSlashCommand[]>;
    /**
     * Wait for agent to become idle (no streaming).
     * Resolves when agent_end event is received.
     */
    waitForIdle(timeout?: number): Promise<void>;
    /**
     * Collect events until agent becomes idle.
     */
    collectEvents(timeout?: number): Promise<AgentEvent[]>;
    /**
     * Send prompt and wait for completion, returning all events.
     */
    promptAndWait(message: string, images?: ImageContent[], timeout?: number): Promise<AgentEvent[]>;
    private handleLine;
    private createProcessExitError;
    private rejectPendingRequests;
    private send;
    private getData;
}
